newsitem.title: UK: CRUDE TANKER CHARTER RATES FIRM IN BRISK ACTIVTY.
newsitem.headline: CRUDE TANKER CHARTER RATES FIRM IN BRISK ACTIVTY.

text.p: Crude oil tanker chartering activity was fairly brisk in most regions on Wednesday with freight rates holding firm, shipbrokers said.
Despite an anticipated increase in demand for Suezmax tonnage, due to the imminent return of Iraqi crude exports, rates for cross-Med voyages for these vessels eased two to five worldscale points.
Fixtures were booked at W75 from Sidi Kreir to Trieste and W72.5 to Med options and Spain.

Three Suezmax vessels were provisionally booked, the Tromso Reliance, Landsort and New Horizon, for mid-August lifting of Iraqi crude at the Turkish port of Ceyhan but no rates were reported or charterers named.
The Concordia 1 was also said to have been booked to lift 300,000 tonne out of Ceyhan to the U.S. Gulf at around W67.5 by U.S. refiner Bayoil.
But this could not be confirmed and some brokers thought the tonnage may have been fixed from the Iraqi port of Mina Al Bakr.
"It's still all up in the air as far as the Iraqi bookings are concerned. It's all 'on subs,' none of the lifters are committing themselves to anything at the moment," a broker said.

Mideast Gulf markets continued to see active trade to the West and East with three ultra-large crude carriers (ULCC's) fixed by Vela from Ras Tanura, two to the U.S. Gulf at a firm W60 and one for Red Sea voyage at W71.
Very large crude carrier (VLCC) tonnage saw the Falcon fixed by KPC from the Mideast to the U.K.-Continent at a steady W65.
Transatlantic rates for million barrel vessels out of West Africa were also stable after recent weakness.

Four vessels, the Bruce, Smart Maple, North Star and one to be named were fixed, three to the U.S. Gulf, with one at around W80, one with 137,000 tonnes at W73.5 and one to East coast Canada at W82.5.
